results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Prerequisite]: Select exactly one stable scope identifier and reuse it for all calls using MEM0_RETRIEVE_MEMORY_LIST (avoid mixing scopes across requests).

[Required] [Step]: List newest items using MEM0_RETRIEVE_MEMORY_LIST (recency) and paginate with page/page_size; continue until a page returns no items or pagination indicates end; collect from response.data.memories (or other observed list keys).

[Optional (if you know a target entity or listing is too broad)] [Next Step]: Retrieve a tighter set using MEM0_GET_MEMORIES_BY_ENTITY or MEM0_SEARCH_MEMORIES_WITH_QUERY_FILTERS, then merge/dedupe by memory identifier.

[Optional (if list output is truncated, you need full fidelity, or you will edit)] [Next Step]: Hydrate selected records using MEM0_RETRIEVE_MEMORY_BY_UNIQUE_IDENTIFIER (dedupe IDs, batch requests); if changes are required, update the confirmed record using MEM0_UPDATE_MEMORY_DETAILS_BY_ID.

[Fallback (if results are empty or scope/entity is unclear)] [Fallback]: Discover valid entities using MEM0_LIST_ENTITIES_WITH_OPTIONAL_ORG_AND_PROJECT_FILTERS, then retry via MEM0_GET_MEMORIES_BY_ENTITY or MEM0_RETRIEVE_MEMORY_LIST in the confirmed scope.
known_pitfalls: [MEM0_RETRIEVE_MEMORY_LIST] Can legitimately return an empty list (e.g., data.count=0 and response.data.memories=[]); treat as a valid empty scope, not an error.
[MEM0_RETRIEVE_MEMORY_LIST] Response shape varies; items may appear under data.memories vs other list keys (e.g., data.results), so parsers should check multiple containers.
[MEM0_RETRIEVE_MEMORY_LIST] Pagination signals vary; response.data.next may be null/absent—treat that as end-of-pagination rather than an error.
[MEM0_RETRIEVE_MEMORY_BY_UNIQUE_IDENTIFIER] Expanding many IDs can trigger HTTP 429; dedupe first, then batch and back off/retry.
[MEM0_UPDATE_MEMORY_DETAILS_BY_ID] Updating with an incorrect/placeholder memory identifier can yield a not-found error; always source the exact identifier from listing/search before updating.

MEM0_RETRIEVE_MEMORY_LIST.description: Retrieves a list of memories, supporting pagination and diverse filtering (e.g., by IDs, metadata, keywords, date ranges); ensure dates are ISO 8601 and `page`/`page_size` (if used) are positive integers. REQUIRED: At least one of agent_id, user_id, app_id, or run_id must be provided.

page.description: The page number for pagination, starting from 1. Default: 1.

app_id.description: The unique identifier of the application associated with the memories. At least one of user_id, agent_id, app_id, or run_id is required.

fields.description: A list of specific field names to consider during filtering. This might involve checking for the existence of these fields or scoping other filters (e.g., keywords) to them.

org_id.description: The unique identifier of the organization to filter memories by. Must be provided together with project_id, or both must be omitted.

run_id.description: The unique identifier of a specific run or session to filter memories by. At least one of user_id, agent_id, app_id, or run_id is required.

user_id.description: The unique identifier of the user whose memories are to be retrieved. At least one of user_id, agent_id, app_id, or run_id is required.

agent_id.description: The unique identifier of the agent associated with the memories to be retrieved. At least one of user_id, agent_id, app_id, or run_id is required.

end_date.description: The end date (inclusive) for filtering memories, typically in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ' or 'YYYY-MM-DD').

keywords.description: Keywords to search for within the memories. The search might be across all text fields or restricted by the `fields` parameter if specified.

metadata.description: A dictionary of key-value pairs to filter memories. Only memories matching all key-value pairs in the provided metadata will be returned.

org_name.description: The name of the organization to filter memories by. This field is deprecated and will be removed in a future version; please use `org_id` instead.

page_size.description: The number of memories to return per page. Default: 100.

categories.description: A list of categories to filter memories by. Memories matching any of the specified categories will be returned.

project_id.description: The unique identifier of the project to filter memories by. Must be provided together with org_id, or both must be omitted.

start_date.description: The start date (inclusive) for filtering memories, typically in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ' or 'YYYY-MM-DD').

project_name.description: The name of the project to filter memories by. This field is deprecated and will be removed in a future version; please use `project_id` instead.

MEM0_RETRIEVE_MEMORY_BY_UNIQUE_IDENTIFIE.description: Retrieves a complete memory entry by its unique identifier; `memory_id` must be valid and for an existing memory.

memory_id.description: Unique identifier of the memory to retrieve.

MEM0_SEARCH_MEMORIES_WITH_QUERY_FILTERS.description: Semantically searches memories using structured filters with an optional natural language query. If query is omitted, defaults to '*' (wildcard) for filter-only searches. Offers options to rerank results, select specific fields, and adjust similarity threshold; any provided `org_id` or `project_id` must reference a valid existing entity.

examples: latest meeting notes with John Doe
query.description: Natural language query for searching memories. The API requires this field to be non-blank, so it defaults to '*' for filter-only searches. Omit or use '*' to retrieve memories matching only the filters without semantic search constraints.

top_k.description: Maximum number of most relevant search results to return.

fields.description: Specific field names to include in returned memory objects (e.g., 'text', 'source', 'metadata.custom_field'). If omitted, all fields are returned.

org_id.description: UUID of the organization to scope the memory search; preferred over `org_name`.

rerank.description: If true, applies a secondary reranking model to initial search results for improved relevance.

filters.description: REQUIRED and cannot be empty - must contain at least one filter condition. Available filter fields: user_id, agent_id, app_id, run_id, created_at, updated_at, categories, keywords. Filters can be provided in two formats: (1) Simple key-value pairs: `{"user_id": "alice"}` for equality matching or `{"created_at": {"gte": "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z"}}` with comparison operators. (2) Wrapped in logical operators: `{"AND": [{"user_id": "alice"}]}` for combining multiple conditions. Comparison operators (lowercase): `in` (matches any value in list), `gte` (>=), `lte` (<=), `gt` (>), `lt` (<), `ne` (not equal), `contains`, `icontains` (case-insensitive). Logical operators (`AND`, `OR`, `NOT`) must be UPPERCASE and take a list of conditions. Use `*` as wildcard to match any value for a field (e.g., `{"user_id": "*"}` to match all users).

org_name.description: Deprecated: Name of the organization to scope the memory search. Use `org_id` instead for improved accuracy and stability.

threshold.description: Minimum similarity threshold for search results (0.0 to 1.0). Higher values return more relevant but fewer results.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to scope the memory search; preferred over `project_name`.

project_name.description: Deprecated: Name of the project to scope the memory search. Use `project_id` instead for improved accuracy and stability.

keyword_search.description: Whether to search for memories based on keywords instead of semantic similarity.

filter_memories.description: Whether to strictly apply all provided metadata filters.
